title: Tenali Raman Tale 125 (Español)

full_text:
During the celebration of his military triumph at Raichur, an exuberant King Krishnadevaraya promised an impoverished, elderly court poet named Somadeva a royal reward of one thousand gold coins and a fertile orchard for his victory ode.
However, in the busy months of administrative reorganization that followed, the King completely forgot his promise.
Whenever poor Somadeva approached the palace, the royal chamberlains turned him away.
Somadeva came weeping to Tenali Raman: 'The Emperor’s promise was my family's only hope, but power forgets the poor.'

Tenali comforted him: 'King Krishnadevaraya is an honorable king; he has merely forgotten. Tomorrow, his memory shall be refreshed.'

The next morning, while King Krishnadevaraya was walking through the royal menagerie with Tenali Raman, they stopped before the enclosure of a newly arrived Bactrian camel.
The King looked at the camel’s large, curved, awkward hump and remarked with amusement:
'Tenali, look at that beast! Why has nature given the camel such an ugly, crooked, bent hump upon its back?'

Tenali Raman looked at the camel, sighed with deep, theatrical sorrow, and said:
'Alas, Your Majesty! That camel was once a great emperor in its past life!'

The King blinked in surprise: 'An emperor? Why is its back crooked then?'

Tenali replied with razor-sharp, devastating wit:
'Because in its past life, Maharaj, that emperor made a solemn promise to a poor poet to give him one thousand gold coins and an orchard, and then completely forgot his royal word!
Every time a king makes a solemn promise to a humble subject and forgets to honor it, heaven bends his spine a little further!
That poor camel’s back is crooked because it is weighed down by the heavy, unfulfilled promises of its past reign!'

King Krishnadevaraya froze.
The words hit the Emperor’s conscience like a thunderbolt!
He remembered his unfulfilled coronation promise to poor poet Somadeva!
The King blushed crimson with shame and profound realization.

The King turned to his chamberlain and commanded in a booming voice:
'Summon poet Somadeva to the palace immediately!
Deliver to him two thousand gold coins—double the promised reward—and the deeds to the finest mango orchard in the province!'

Somadeva was brought to court and showered with royal honors.
King Krishnadevaraya embraced Tenali Raman with tears of gratitude:
'Tenali, thou hast saved my spine from bending like a camel’s back!
A king who forgets his promises to the poor forgets his honor before heaven.'

The court celebrated Tenali’s brilliant, compassionate wit, which held power accountable to truth.
moral: A ruler who makes promises to the poor must fulfill his sacred word; a camel's hump serves as an unforgettable reminder. [ES]
